comparison: Traditional face-to-face instruction; undergraduate programs compared to postgraduate programs
exposure: Transition to digital/online learning environments and technological adoption during COVID-19
outcome: Student satisfaction measured through Net Promoter Score (NPS)
population: Higher education students (undergraduate and postgraduate) during the COVID-19 pandemic
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines how the COVID-19 pandemic-driven transition to digital learning affected student satisfaction in higher education, as measured by Net Promoter Score (NPS), comparing experiences across different educational modalities (traditional vs. digital) and program levels (undergraduate vs. postgraduate).

comparison: Other leadership styles (e.g., transformational or transactional leadership) or absence of servant leadership
exposure: Servant leadership practiced by school principals and educational leaders
outcome: Physical and mental health outcomes, behavioral outcomes, teacher performance, harmonious work environment, teacher well-being, job satisfaction, professional engagement, stress reduction, and innovative teaching methods
population: Teachers in educational organizations across diverse geographical regions including Asia, Europe, North America, and Africa
research_question: This systematic review examines how servant leadership benefits teachers in educational settings, exploring its effects on teachers' physical and mental health outcomes, behavioral outcomes, performance, and the creation of harmonious work environments compared to other leadership approaches or absence of servant leadership.

comparison: Varying definitions and interpretations across different scholarly perspectives, disciplines, and contexts
exposure: Conceptual and definitional frameworks used to characterize extremism and religious extremism
outcome: Identification of recurring themes (belief, behaviour, absence of universal definition) and sub-themes (uncompromised views, biased interpretation, specific society, violation of true teaching) in extremism definitions
population: Academic literature and scholarly articles addressing definitions of extremism and religious extremism published between 2018 and December 2023
research_question: This systematic review examines how extremism and religious extremism are defined across academic literature, exploring the various conceptual frameworks, thematic elements, and interpretive patterns that characterize these phenomena, with the aim of identifying common definitional features and addressing the lack of a universal standard definition.

comparison: Comparison between professional groups (nurses vs. physicians) and by gender (women vs. men)
exposure: Occupational exposure to traumatic events in emergency department settings
outcome: Prevalence of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) meeting diagnostic criteria
population: Emergency department personnel (nurses and physicians) in Canada and the USA
research_question: This systematic review examines the prevalence of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) among emergency department personnel (nurses and physicians) in Canada and the USA, and explores whether prevalence differs by profession (nurses vs. physicians) and gender.

comparison: Successful versus unsuccessful digital health implementation contexts
exposure: Digital transformation implementation in healthcare (including telemedicine, electronic health records, mobile health applications, and other digital health technologies)
outcome: Barriers to digital transformation implementation (including technological infrastructure limitations, data security and privacy concerns, lack of physical examination capability, organizational barriers, financial barriers, and behavioral resistance)
population: Healthcare stakeholders in India including healthcare providers, patients, and health systems
research_question: This systematic review aims to identify the potential barriers to implementing digital transformation in the health sector of India, examining the challenges that impede successful adoption of digital health technologies across healthcare settings in the country.

comparison: Pre-pandemic period or absence of lockdown conditions
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic and associated lockdown measures (full and partial lockdowns)
outcome: Forms of domestic violence (physical, economic, psychological, emotional, verbal, sexual violence, control and humiliation, bullying, online abuse, harassment, neglect) and causes of domestic violence (economic, socio-cultural, and psychological factors)
population: Women in Jordan who experienced domestic violence during the COVID-19 pandemic
research_question: This systematic review explores the forms and causes of domestic violence against women in Jordan during the COVID-19 pandemic, examining how economic, social, and health-related effects of the pandemic and associated lockdowns contributed to increased domestic violence cases.

comparison: European versus non-European educational contexts; active versus passive use of AVT; different AVT modes (subtitling, dubbing, audio description)
intervention: Pedagogical use of audiovisual translation (AVT) modes including both active use (didactic subtitling, dubbing, audio description) and passive use (reception of existing AVT materials) in language education
outcome: Research trends and characteristics, language learning outcomes including linguistic skills (vocabulary, listening, reading) and integrated/transferable skills, geographical distribution of research, and identification of knowledge gaps in the field
population: Language learners across various educational levels, primarily in higher education settings, with a focus on English language learners
research_question: This scoping review aims to map the current research landscape of the pedagogical use of audiovisual translation (AVT) in language education, examining key characteristics and trends in publication characteristics, contextual factors, and research designs, while identifying knowledge gaps and comparing research between European and non-European contexts.

comparison: Pre-pandemic living and working conditions of migrants; general non-migrant population
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic lockdown conditions, circular/reverse migration, displacement from work locations, poor relief camp conditions, financial crisis, and travel restrictions
outcome: Psychosocial issues, mental health outcomes, financial distress, quality of relief camp conditions, access to facilities and rations, and overall wellbeing of migrant workers and their families
population: Internal migrant workers in India, including daily-wage laborers, women, and children migrants
research_question: This systematic review examines the multiple adversities and hardships experienced by migrant workers in India during the COVID-19 pandemic and lockdown, including the socio-psychological impact of circular (reverse) migration, compared to their pre-pandemic conditions and the general population.

comparison: Countries or time periods with lower ICT adoption/usage levels; developed countries compared to developing countries
exposure: Information and communication technologies (ICTs) adoption and usage, including mobile technology
outcome: Economic performance indicators including economic growth and productivity
population: Countries (both developed and developing nations)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the relationship between information and communication technologies (ICTs) and economic performance at the country level, examining whether ICTs have positive or negative effects on economic growth, and exploring how factors such as country development status (developed vs. developing), type of ICT (e.g., mobile technology), sample size, and time period influence this relationship.

comparison: Firms with varying levels of BDA adoption, organizational agility, and across different national cultural contexts
exposure: Big data analytics (BDA) capability and utilization
outcome: Firm performance (FP) and organizational agility (OA)
population: Firms that have adopted big data analytics
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether big data analytics (BDA) improves firm performance, and specifically examines whether organizational agility serves as a mediating mechanism in the BDA-firm performance relationship, while also exploring how national culture moderates these relationships across firms in different countries.

comparison: Traditional or non-ML-based cybercrime prevention approaches
exposure: Machine learning-based cyber-attack prevention techniques (including supervised and unsupervised methods such as support vector machine and naive Bayes classification)
outcome: Effectiveness of ML techniques in preventing cybercrimes, identification of most frequently applied ML practices, and technical challenges in implementation
population: Online retail companies and e-tailing platforms
research_question: This systematic literature review investigates which machine learning-based techniques are most frequently applied and effective for preventing cyber-attacks in the online retail industry, examining the current state of ML prevention algorithms and their implementation in e-tailing contexts.

comparison: Conventional resident population estimates that capture population at a single point in time without accounting for temporary mobility
exposure: Various data sources and estimation methods for temporary populations, including mobile phone data, symptomatic data, surveys, and other geolocated data sources
outcome: Identification of estimation approaches, data types, methodological frameworks, geographic and temporal coverage, reproducibility, and the current state of the art in temporary population estimation
population: Temporary populations including visitors, commuters, tourists, and other mobile populations that cause short-term fluctuations in local population counts
research_question: This systematic review examines the empirical literature on temporary population estimation methods to identify the contemporary state of the art, including the data sources, methodologies, geographic coverage, and temporal units used to estimate populations that fluctuate due to temporary mobility such as commuting, tourism, and seasonal movements.

comparison: Control conditions (including standard behavioural weight management interventions)
intervention: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based weight management interventions
outcome: Percentage weight change from baseline to 12 months after intervention end
population: Adults with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²)
research_question: This individual participant data meta-analysis investigates whether baseline eating behaviour traits (including emotional eating, uncontrolled eating, external eating, internal disinhibition, and restraint) moderate the effect of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based weight management interventions on weight loss outcomes in adults with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²) compared to control conditions.

comparison: Lower/disadvantaged socioeconomic position groups
exposure: Socioeconomic position (SEP) measured at any age across the life course, including education, occupational social class, income, area-level SEP, and composite measures of material living standards
outcome: Body composition measures in adulthood including fat mass, fat-free mass, lean mass, fat mass ratio, and fat distribution (measured using direct techniques such as dual x-ray absorptiometry)
population: General adult population from studies across high-income and middle-income countries
research_question: This systematic review examines the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) measured across the life course (in childhood and adulthood) and body composition measures (fat mass, fat-free mass, lean mass, and fat distribution) in adulthood, and assesses whether these associations differ by sex, birth cohort, country income level, and SEP measure used.

comparison: Incrementally layered conventional resin composite restorations (applied in increments of ≤2 mm)
intervention: Bulk-fill resin composite restoration technique (applied in layers of 4-5 mm thickness)
outcome: Clinical performance parameters including retention, recurrent/secondary caries, marginal discoloration/staining, marginal adaptation/integrity, fracture, postoperative sensitivity, anatomic form, color match, and surface texture/roughness
population: Permanent teeth requiring Class I and Class II direct resin composite restorations
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether bulk-fill resin composite restorations demonstrate comparable or superior clinical effectiveness compared to incrementally layered conventional resin composite restorations for Class I and Class II cavities in permanent teeth, as measured by clinical parameters including retention, secondary caries, marginal adaptation, fracture, and postoperative sensitivity.

comparison: Traditional classroom teaching methods (lectures, slides, and conventional educational approaches)
intervention: Virtual reality (VR) technology-based learning materials and environments (including non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive VR)
outcome: Student creativity enhancement, including the ability to generate novel ideas, innovate, engage in abstract thinking, problem-solving, and creative expression
population: College students in higher education across various majors (including art design, engineering, and education)
research_question: This systematic literature review examines the trends, types of learning materials, research methods, and developmental outcomes associated with using virtual reality (VR) technology to enhance creativity among college students in higher education settings compared to traditional educational approaches.

comparison: Traditional banking operations without fintech integration or lower levels of fintech adoption
exposure: Financial technology (fintech) adoption and development, measured at bank-level (financial innovation, use of online channels), country-level (digital finance index, commercial bank digital transformation index), and through fintech keywords (social media platforms, documents)
outcome: Bank risk measures including insolvency risk, credit risk, market risk, and liquidity risk, with consideration of mediating variables (operational efficiency, capital adequacy ratio, net interest margin) and moderating variables (digital transformation, financial regulation, economic uncertainty)
population: Commercial banks and banking institutions globally
research_question: This systematic literature review examines how financial technology (fintech) adoption and development impacts various dimensions of bank risk, including insolvency risk, credit risk, market risk, and liquidity risk, in commercial banks compared to traditional banking operations without fintech integration.

comparison: Pre-intervention digital competence levels or control conditions without digital competence interventions
intervention: Educational intervention strategies designed to improve digital competence
outcome: Digital competence levels (including digital literacy, ICT skills, information literacy, media literacy, and related 21st-century skills), research trends, methodological approaches, and intervention effectiveness
population: Adolescents and young adults aged 15-25 years (including secondary students, university students, and those in vocational training or employment)
research_question: This scoping review examines the research landscape of digital competence in adolescents and young adults aged 15-25, investigating what concomitant variables (determining factors and consequences) have been studied, what methodological approaches are commonly used in measurement research, and what intervention strategies have been evaluated to foster digital competence in this population.

comparison: Expected standards of effective global health governance and pandemic response leadership
exposure: Criticisms of WHO's COVID-19 response including delays in response, communication failures, vaccine equity issues, global coordination challenges, governance limitations, and trust and transparency concerns
outcome: Thematic categorization of critiques across six key themes: delays in response, communication failures, vaccine equity, global coordination, governance limitations, and trust and transparency, with identification of reform recommendations
population: Academic literature and peer-reviewed research studies examining WHO's COVID-19 pandemic response
research_question: This scoping review systematically examines and categorizes how criticisms of the World Health Organization's COVID-19 pandemic response have been framed across multiple stakeholders, including governments, public health professionals, media, and the public, to identify key themes related to governance challenges, geopolitical tensions, and trust-related concerns that shaped narratives surrounding the WHO's pandemic management.

comparison: Different urethroplasty techniques compared against each other (staged vs. one-stage, augmented vs. non-augmented)
intervention: Urethroplasty techniques (staged urethroplasty, one-stage urethroplasty with or without augmentation, buccal mucosa grafts)
outcome: Urethral complication recurrence rates (strictures and fistulas), patient-reported outcomes, need for secondary surgical interventions
population: Transgender men who underwent urethral lengthening as part of phalloplasty or metoidioplasty and developed urethral complications requiring urethroplasty
research_question: This systematic review examines the outcomes of urethroplasty following urethral lengthening in transgender men, comparing different surgical techniques (staged vs. one-stage urethroplasty, with or without augmentation) to determine recurrence rates of urethral complications such as strictures and fistulas.

comparison: Different phalloplasty techniques compared (radial artery free flap vs anterolateral thigh flap)
intervention: Phalloplasty reconstruction (radial artery free flap and anterolateral thigh flap techniques)
outcome: Urinary function (standing micturition), sexual function (sexual activity), complication rates (urethral strictures, fistulae), tactile recovery, donor site morbidity, and patient satisfaction
population: Men who have undergone partial or total penectomy for penile cancer (cisgender males post-penectomy)
research_question: This narrative review summarizes the available evidence on phalloplasty following penectomy for penile cancer, examining the effectiveness of different surgical techniques (primarily radial artery free flap and anterolateral thigh flap) in restoring urinary and sexual function, complication rates, and patient satisfaction outcomes.

comparison: Delayed inflatable penile prosthesis insertion
intervention: Early inflatable penile prosthesis implantation versus delayed inflatable penile prosthesis implantation
outcome: Complication rates (edema, infection, distal perforations), pain relief, priapism resolution, penile shortening prevention, and time to sexual activity resumption
population: Patients with ischemic priapism requiring penile prosthesis implantation
research_question: This narrative review compares the outcomes of early versus delayed inflatable penile prosthesis implantation in patients with ischemic priapism, examining whether early insertion offers superior results in terms of complication rates, pain relief, priapism resolution, penile length preservation, and return to sexual activity.

comparison: Comparisons across time periods, countries, databases, impact factor categories, disciplines, and sub-disciplines
exposure: Journal characteristics including publication year, country, database indexation, impact factor, discipline, and sub-discipline
outcome: Percentage of Instructions to Authors addressing research integrity topics (authorship, conflicts of interest, data sharing, ethics approval, funding disclosure, and ICMJE Uniform Requirements for Manuscripts)
population: Scholarly journals' Instructions to Authors documents
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines how frequently scholarly journals' Instructions to Authors address key research integrity topics (authorship, conflicts of interest, data sharing, ethics approval, funding disclosure, and ICMJE Uniform Requirements) and identifies factors that explain heterogeneity in coverage, including time period, country, database indexation, impact factor, discipline, and sub-discipline.

comparison: Any control arm (including standard care, placebo, or usual care)
intervention: Hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine treatment
outcome: All-cause mortality
population: Patients with COVID-19
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to estimate the effects of hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine treatment on all-cause mortality in patients with COVID-19 compared to control arms, synthesizing evidence from all available randomized clinical trials including both published and unpublished data.

comparison: Index cases (ascertained through clinical presentation or symptom reporting)
exposure: Case ascertainment method (index case vs. secondary case identification through contact tracing)
outcome: Clinical severity measures including proportion with fever, proportion symptomatic, hospitalization rates, and fatality rates
population: COVID-19 index cases and their secondary cases identified through contact tracing studies
research_question: This systematic review examines whether secondary cases identified through contact tracing exhibit different clinical severity profiles (including symptomatic proportion, hospitalization rates, and fatality rates) compared to index cases in COVID-19, and whether this difference can be used to estimate the proportion of missed index cases and reduce ascertainment bias in emerging infectious disease severity estimates.

comparison: No vegetable consumption or lowest category of vegetable consumption
exposure: Vegetable consumption (ranging from no consumption to theoretical minimum risk exposure level of 306-372 g daily)
outcome: Risk of ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, type 2 diabetes, and esophageal cancer
population: General adult population
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the association between vegetable consumption and the risk of chronic diseases including ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, type 2 diabetes, and esophageal cancer in the general population, comparing higher vegetable intake levels to no or low vegetable consumption, while also evaluating the quality of evidence supporting these associations using a Bayesian meta-regression approach.

comparison: Lower levels of unprocessed red meat consumption or no consumption (0 g per day as reference)
exposure: Unprocessed red meat consumption (measured in grams per day)
outcome: Disease incidence and mortality for six health outcomes: colorectal cancer, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and hemorrhagic stroke
population: General adult population from prospective observational cohort studies
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the association between unprocessed red meat consumption and six chronic disease outcomes (colorectal cancer, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and hemorrhagic stroke) in the general adult population, using a novel burden of proof methodology to quantify both the dose-response relationships and the strength of evidence underlying these associations.

comparison: Placebo or appropriate comparator (control condition)
intervention: Acute glucagon administration
outcome: Ad libitum meal energy intake, energy expenditure, subjective appetite, circulating glucose concentrations, and circulating insulin concentrations
population: Adults without diabetes
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to estimate the mean effect of acute glucagon administration on components of energy balance (energy intake, energy expenditure, subjective appetite) and glucose homeostasis (glucose and insulin concentrations) in adults without diabetes compared to placebo or appropriate control conditions.

comparison: Reference systolic blood pressure level of 100 mm Hg
exposure: Elevated systolic blood pressure (SBP) levels ranging from 100 to 200 mm Hg
outcome: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) risk including mortality, prevalent cases, and disability-adjusted life years
population: General adult population including individuals with and without pre-existing cardiovascular disease or hypertension
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the continuous dose-response relationship between elevated systolic blood pressure (SBP) and the risk of ischemic heart disease (IHD), examining whether higher SBP levels are associated with increased IHD risk compared to lower SBP levels (reference at 100 mm Hg), using evidence from both observational cohort studies and randomized controlled trials.

comparison: Traditional risk assessment methods
exposure: Application of artificial intelligence methods (machine learning, deep learning, large language models) for risk prediction
outcome: Prediction performance for safety risks (adverse drug events), efficacy risks (treatment effect estimation), and operational risks (phase transition prediction), measured by metrics such as AUROC
population: Clinical trials across various phases and therapeutic conditions
research_question: This scoping review examines how artificial intelligence methods are applied to predict and assess various types of risks (safety, efficacy, and operational) in clinical trials, evaluating the effectiveness of different AI algorithms and data sources compared to traditional risk assessment approaches.

comparison: Traditional risk score models and comparison between unimodal versus multimodal AI approaches, as well as internal versus external validation methods
exposure: Various risk factors and data modalities including electronic health records, multi-omics data, medical imaging, behavioral/wellness, and environmental data used in AI-based prediction models
outcome: Type 2 diabetes mellitus risk prediction performance measured by discrimination (area under the curve/AUC), calibration, and model generalizability
population: Individuals at risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus (general population in longitudinal studies)
research_question: This scoping review examines the current state of artificial intelligence-based methods, including machine learning and deep learning models, for predicting the risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus in individuals, evaluating the data modalities used (electronic health records, multi-omics, medical imaging), model performance metrics, validation approaches, and the key risk predictors identified by these models.

comparison: Pre-EMR implementation status or hospitals without EMR systems
intervention: Electronic medical record (EMR) implementation in hospital settings
outcome: Economic impacts including cost savings, cost-benefit ratios, patient outcomes, population health improvements, healthcare efficiency, and alignment with quadruple aims of healthcare
population: Hospitals implementing electronic medical records (EMRs)
research_question: This scoping review examines how electronic medical record (EMR) implementations in hospital settings have been evaluated using cost-benefit analysis approaches internationally, aiming to understand the economic frameworks used to assess the value and impacts of digital hospital implementations.

comparison: Different LLM architectures and approaches (pre-transformer models, encoder-based models, various reporting granularities), as well as internal versus external validation performance
exposure: Application of large language model (LLM) based natural language processing approaches, including pre-transformer and encoder-based models such as BERT
outcome: Information extraction performance from radiology reports, including named entity recognition, relation extraction, template filling accuracy, generalizability across external datasets, and comparability of approaches
population: Radiology reports (free-text clinical documentation from radiological imaging examinations, particularly CT, MRI, and thoracic imaging)
research_question: This scoping review examines the current state of research on Large Language Model (LLM) based approaches for information extraction from radiology reports, investigating how these models perform in extracting structured clinical information from free-text radiological documentation and what challenges affect their generalizability and external validation.

comparison: Standard care or no smartphone application support
intervention: Native smartphone applications for caregiver support
outcome: Usability, caregiver burden, quality of life, and other process and health outcomes related to caregiver support
population: Informal caregivers (family or friends) of chronically ill adults living in the community
research_question: This scoping review investigates the nature and extent of native smartphone applications designed to support informal caregivers of chronically ill patients living in the community, examining what is known in the literature about these applications across various common chronic conditions including heart disease, stroke, cancer, chronic obstructive respiratory disease, asthma, diabetes, Alzheimer's disease or other dementia, rheumatoid arthritis, hypertension, and mood or anxiety disorders.

comparison: Different XR modalities (VR vs AR vs MR), tangible vs intangible cultural heritage applications, and various emotional stimulation approaches (interface-driven vs other methods)
exposure: Extended reality (XR) technologies including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR) with emotional design elements
outcome: Emotional engagement, emotional interaction quality, user cognition enhancement, and effectiveness of cultural heritage preservation and transmission
population: Users engaging with cultural heritage content through extended reality (XR) technologies
research_question: This systematic review investigates how immersive extended reality (XR) technologies are currently applied to create emotionally interactive experiences in cultural heritage preservation, what types of emotional interactions users experience through XR applications, and how emotional interaction design in XR can be optimized to enhance user cognition and engagement with intangible cultural heritage.

comparison: Traditional predictive models and conventional methods for medication safety
intervention: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) for drug-drug interaction identification, clinical decision support, and pharmacovigilance
outcome: Effectiveness in early identification and classification of adverse drug events, drug-drug interaction prediction, and support for medication management decision-making
population: Patients in medical care settings at risk of medication-related harm
research_question: This scoping review evaluates the scope and effectiveness of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) in reducing medication-related harm, including their applications in drug-drug interaction identification, clinical decision support, and pharmacovigilance compared to conventional methods.

comparison: traditional mental health interventions or standard care
intervention: large language models (LLMs) for mental health applications
outcome: model performance and clinical effectiveness in mental health care delivery
population: individuals requiring mental health care services
research_question: This scoping review examines the applications and effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in mental health care for generative tasks such as clinical assistance, counseling, therapy, and emotional support, evaluating their performance and clinical effectiveness compared to traditional mental health interventions.

comparison: Traditional physical therapy or standard care conditions
intervention: Virtual walking interventions including passive observing moving, arm swing locomotion, and foot tracking locomotion using virtual reality technologies
outcome: Pain reduction, physical function (mobility and muscle strength), depression, psychological well-being, feasibility, acceptability, and neurological mechanisms (somatosensory cortex activation)
population: Individuals with mobility disabilities, primarily those with spinal cord injuries, lower back pain, and lower limb pain
research_question: This scoping review aims to synthesize evidence on the characteristics, effectiveness, feasibility, and neurological mechanisms of virtual walking interventions on health-related outcomes in individuals with mobility disabilities, particularly those with spinal cord injuries, lower back pain, and lower limb pain.

comparison: Comparison across different types of data, predictive models, and robustness concepts identified in the literature
exposure: Different types of perturbations and variations affecting machine learning model performance (including adversarial attacks, environmental changes, and deployment conditions)
outcome: Identification and classification of eight general concepts of robustness for machine learning models in healthcare, and their distribution across data types and model types
population: Machine learning models and AI-based solutions deployed in healthcare settings for decision support
research_question: This scoping review aims to identify and map the various concepts of robustness addressed in the literature for machine learning models used in healthcare decision support, examining how these robustness concepts differ across types of data and predictive models.

comparison: Traditional in-person rehabilitation or no rehabilitation
intervention: Artificial intelligence-driven home-based virtual rehabilitation programs
outcome: Rehabilitation outcomes including physical and mental functioning, exercise quality assessment, and patient health outcomes
population: Adult patients living in the community requiring rehabilitation
research_question: This scoping review explores the applications and effectiveness of incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into home-based virtual rehabilitation (VRehab) programs for adult patients living in the community, examining how AI-driven VRehab compares to traditional rehabilitation approaches in improving physical and mental health outcomes.

comparison: Traditional healthcare delivery without AI-based technology or standard care practices
intervention: Artificial intelligence technologies in healthcare (including clinical decision support systems, treatment planning and triage assistants, health chatbots, machine learning, natural language processing, and image processing)
outcome: Effects on healthcare provision (diagnosis, treatment, health outcomes, provider/patient time, costs), user experiences (acceptance, perceived usefulness, trust, feasibility), reliability, workflow impacts, user friendliness, and context-appropriateness of AI tools
population: Healthcare systems, healthcare providers, and patients in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs)
research_question: This systematic scoping review aims to evaluate the scope, nature, and effectiveness of artificial intelligence technologies applied to healthcare systems in low- and middle-income countries, examining their effects on healthcare provision (diagnosis, treatment, health outcomes, costs), the experiences of providers and patients with AI-based healthcare technology, and the key elements that support or challenge AI implementation in LMIC healthcare contexts.

comparison: Self-report or objective ground-truth methods (traditional dietary assessment tools including 24-h recalls, food records, and food frequency questionnaires)
exposure: Use of wearable devices/sensors (including accelerometers and multi-sensor systems) for automatic eating activity detection
outcome: Eating activity detection performance measured by accuracy, F1-score, and other evaluation metrics; eating outcomes including meal microstructure, meal duration, eating rate, chewing frequency, and food choices
population: General population including youth and adults in free-living/naturalistic settings
research_question: This scoping review aims to catalog and summarize the current use of wearable devices and sensors that automatically detect eating-related activity in free-living (naturalistic) research settings, identifying the sensor types, sample sizes, ground-truth validation methods, eating outcome measures, and evaluation metrics used to assess these wearable-based eating detection systems.

comparison: Variation across different quality assessment approaches and criteria used in published studies
exposure: Quality criteria and evaluation frameworks used to assess mobile health apps
outcome: Identification and categorization of quality criteria used for mobile app evaluation, including user engagement functions, behavior change features, technical features, and usability measures
population: Mobile health applications designed for patients with chronic diseases
research_question: This scoping review examines what quality criteria are used to assess mobile health applications designed to support chronic disease management, synthesizing the range of evaluation approaches employed across studies that review app quality.

comparison: Traditional statistical and predictive models (log-linear, time-varying function, dose-response function, power function, Eyring and Arrhenius models)
exposure: Application of various machine learning models to corrosion prediction tasks
outcome: Predictive performance metrics of machine learning models for corrosion rate prediction across different corrosion topics
population: Published research articles on machine learning applied to electrochemical corrosion prediction with comparable performance metrics
research_question: This systematic review examines which machine learning models have been applied to predict electrochemical corrosion and how well they perform across different corrosion topics, compared to traditional predictive models, in order to guide corrosion experts and model developers in their applications of ML to corrosion research.

comparison: Adequacy of research design and reporting standards for real-world implementation
intervention: Preventive digital health interventions (DHIs) for mental health, including universal, selective, and indicated prevention approaches
outcome: Quality of reporting on user co-design involvement, barriers and facilitators to implementation, financial costs, human support provision, and factors supporting successful adoption into real-world practice
population: Children and young people, including adolescents and those aged ≤10 years
research_question: This scoping review examines how well the research literature on preventive digital mental health interventions for children and young people describes factors related to development, evaluation, and implementation that are necessary to support real-world adoption, including co-design involvement, barriers and facilitators, and financial costs.

comparison: conventional diagnostic methods and current standards of care
exposure: artificial intelligence models and methods
outcome: diagnostic and predictive accuracy (sensitivity and specificity)
population: patients with endometriosis or suspected endometriosis
research_question: This scoping review examines how artificial intelligence methods have been applied to address clinical problems in endometriosis, including diagnosis, prediction, and management, and evaluates the diagnostic and predictive accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of these AI models compared to conventional diagnostic methods.

comparison: standard care or no intervention
intervention: fully automated conversational agents (including chatbots and embodied agents)
outcome: emotional component of mental health (anxiety, depression, psychological distress)
population: children, adolescents, and young people
research_question: This scoping review examines the current state of research on fully automated conversational agents (CAs) as interventions for improving the emotional component of mental health (including anxiety, depression, and psychological distress) among young people, assessing their technological characteristics, acceptability, usability, and clinical efficacy.

comparison: Absence of mHealth application support or traditional caregiver support methods
intervention: Mobile health (mHealth) applications with functionalities including tracking, task management, monitoring, caregiver mental support, education, and communication platforms
outcome: Caregiver empowerment through mHealth application functionalities (tracking, task management, monitoring, mental support, education, and communication capabilities)
population: Caregivers of Alzheimer's Disease patients
research_question: This scoping review examines the published academic literature on mobile health (mHealth) applications designed to support caregivers of Alzheimer's Disease patients, identifying the functionalities and features these applications provide to empower caregivers in managing patient care.

comparison: traditional clinical documentation methods or manual scribes
exposure: digital scribe systems using ASR and NLP technologies
outcome: technical validity, clinical validity, usability, and clinical utility of digital scribes
population: clinical practice settings and healthcare providers using digital documentation systems
research_question: This scoping review examines the current development status and performance of digital scribes using automatic speech recognition and natural language processing for automating clinical documentation in healthcare settings, and identifies gaps in technical validity, clinical validity, and utility assessment.

comparison: traditional drug development and repurposing methods without EHR data
exposure: electronic health records data utilization in computational drug repurposing
outcome: identification of new drug-disease associations and therapeutic indications
population: approved or investigational drugs and their potential new therapeutic applications
research_question: This scoping review examines how computational drug repurposing methods utilize electronic health records (EHRs) data to identify new therapeutic applications for approved or investigational drugs, focusing on the data types, processing methods, and validation approaches used in recent research.

comparison: Placebo, best available treatment, or other JAK inhibitors (network comparison)
intervention: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors including ruxolitinib, fedratinib, pacritinib, and momelotinib
outcome: Spleen volume reduction, total symptom score reduction, anemia events, and thrombocytopenia events
population: Patients with myelofibrosis (including primary myelofibrosis and secondary myelofibrosis post-polycythemia vera or post-essential thrombocythemia)
research_question: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluates and compares the efficacy and tolerability of different Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors (ruxolitinib, fedratinib, pacritinib, and momelotinib) in patients with myelofibrosis, assessing their effects on spleen volume reduction, total symptom score reduction, and hematological adverse events including anemia and thrombocytopenia.

comparison: Observation or placebo
intervention: Early therapeutic intervention with anti-myeloma regimens
outcome: Progression-free survival, time-to-progression to symptomatic multiple myeloma, overall survival, and serious adverse events
population: Patients with intermediate or high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether early therapeutic intervention improves clinical outcomes including progression-free survival, time-to-progression, and overall survival in patients with intermediate or high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma compared to observation or placebo.

comparison: Patients with solid cancers and healthy individuals; comparisons across different hematologic malignancy subtypes and treatment modalities (including CAR-T cell therapy, B-cell targeted therapies, and JAK inhibitors)
intervention: SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (complete vaccination with mRNA vaccines, ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, or Ad26.COV2.S, and booster doses)
outcome: Seroconversion rate, neutralizing antibody development rate, cellular immune response rate, and combined humoral and cellular immunity failure rate
population: Patients with hematologic malignancies (including lymphoid and myeloid malignancies)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the immunogenicity and factors associated with impaired immune responses following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and booster doses in patients with hematologic malignancies, examining seroconversion rates, neutralizing antibody development, and cellular immune responses across various disease subtypes and treatment modalities compared to expected responses in immunocompetent individuals or solid cancer patients.

comparison: General-purpose LLM models versus advanced prompting strategies; different levels of deployment maturity
exposure: Application of Large Language Models (LLMs), predominantly ChatGPT, in dental practice
outcome: Applications of LLMs in dentistry, evaluation metrics used, prompting strategies employed, and deployment levels of LLMs in dental practice
population: Dental practice settings and dental specialties
research_question: This scoping review systematically evaluates the current literature on the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in dentistry, examining their diverse use cases, evaluation metrics, prompting strategies employed, and deployment levels to understand the state of LLM integration in dental practice.

comparison: Not explicitly defined; implicit comparison with general population or those receiving integrated dental-memory clinic services
exposure: Dementia diagnosis and community-dwelling status
outcome: Oral health practices, oral health-related beliefs/views, oral health-related experiences, oral and dental health status, capacity for self-performed oral hygiene, and perceptions of oral health and quality of life
population: Community-dwelling older adults living with dementia and their carers
research_question: This rapid review examines the oral health practices, beliefs/views, and experiences of community-dwelling older adults living with dementia and their carers, exploring what they do to maintain oral health, how they perceive oral health care, and what changes occur throughout their dementia journey.

comparison: Healthy controls
exposure: Blood-based microRNA expression levels (plasma or serum miRNAs)
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy for colorectal cancer detection measured by sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC)
population: Patients with colorectal cancer and healthy controls
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether blood-based microRNAs (miRNAs) in plasma or serum can serve as effective biomarkers for the diagnosis of colorectal cancer, comparing patients with CRC to healthy controls to assess their potential as a non-invasive screening tool.

comparison: Patients without CDKN2A hypermethylation (normal methylation status)
exposure: CDKN2A promoter hypermethylation
outcome: Overall survival, lymphovascular invasion, lymph node metastasis, and proximal tumour location
population: Patients with colorectal cancer
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether CDKN2A promoter hypermethylation is associated with overall survival and clinicopathological features in patients with colorectal cancer, aiming to determine its prognostic value compared to patients without CDKN2A hypermethylation.

comparison: Lower levels of red and processed meat consumption (dose-response analysis using intake increments)
exposure: Red and processed meat consumption (measured in grams per week or servings per week)
outcome: Risk of ovarian cancer (measured as relative risk)
population: Women (general female population from prospective cohort studies)
research_question: This dose-response meta-analysis investigates whether red and processed meat consumption is associated with the risk of ovarian cancer in women, examining the relationship between specific intake increments and cancer risk based on prospective cohort studies.

comparison: Traditional histopathological examination (reference standard)
exposure: One-step nucleic acid amplification (OSNA) assay for intra-operative sentinel lymph node biopsy
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy measures including sensitivity, specificity, positive likelihood ratio, negative likelihood ratio, diagnostic odds ratio, and area under the sROC curve for detecting sentinel lymph node metastasis
population: Breast cancer patients undergoing sentinel lymph node biopsy
research_question: This meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of one-step nucleic acid amplification (OSNA) assay as an intra-operative method for detecting sentinel lymph node metastasis in breast cancer patients compared to traditional histopathological examination.

comparison: Negative peritoneal cytology (control group)
exposure: Positive peritoneal cytology
outcome: Cancer recurrence and lymph node metastasis
population: Patients with cervical cancer
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether positive peritoneal cytology is associated with increased risk of recurrence and lymph node metastasis in patients with cervical cancer compared to those with negative peritoneal cytology.

comparison: Pathologic tumor size measurement (gold standard), and alternative tests including ultrasound, mammography, and clinical examination
exposure: MRI measurement of residual tumor size after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
outcome: Agreement between imaging-measured and pathologic tumor size, assessed by mean differences, limits of agreement, percentage agreement, and correlation coefficients
population: Breast cancer patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy
research_question: This meta-analysis examines the agreement between MRI-measured residual tumor size and pathologic tumor size in breast cancer patients after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and compares MRI's accuracy with alternative imaging tests including ultrasound, mammography, and clinical examination.

comparison: Different chemotherapy regimens compared across randomised trial arms
intervention: First-line chemotherapy regimens (including gemcitabine-containing therapies and targeted agents)
outcome: Correlations between efficacy endpoints (median progression-free survival ratio, response rate, disease control rate) and overall survival (OS), including surrogate threshold effect (STE)
population: Patients with advanced biliary tract cancer (ABTC) receiving first-line chemotherapy
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether progression-free survival (PFS), response rate, and disease control rate can serve as valid surrogate endpoints for overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced biliary tract cancer receiving first-line chemotherapy, by examining the correlations between these efficacy endpoints across randomised trials.

comparison: Non-use of aspirin after colorectal cancer diagnosis
exposure: Aspirin use after diagnosis of colorectal cancer
outcome: All-cause mortality and colorectal cancer-specific mortality
population: Patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether the use of aspirin after diagnosis of colorectal cancer is associated with improved patient survival, specifically examining the relationship between post-diagnosis aspirin use and both all-cause mortality and colorectal cancer-specific mortality.

comparison: Non-users of COX inhibitors
exposure: Cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibitors use, including aspirin and non-aspirin COX inhibitors
outcome: Risk of esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) or high-grade dysplasia (HGD)
population: Patients with Barrett's esophagus
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether the use of cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibitors, including aspirin and non-aspirin COX inhibitors, is associated with a reduced risk of developing esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) or high-grade dysplasia (HGD) in patients with Barrett's esophagus compared to non-users.

comparison: standard care or no specific comparison (single-arm studies)
intervention: autologous anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy
outcome: overall survival, event-free survival, and overall response rate
population: pediatric and adult patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the long-term efficacy of autologous anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy in pediatric and adult patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, examining factors that influence treatment outcomes including overall survival, event-free survival, and response rates.

comparison: Metabolically healthy normal-weight individuals (MHNW)
exposure: Metabolic obesity phenotypes (metabolically unhealthy overweight/obese, metabolically unhealthy normal-weight, metabolically healthy overweight/obese)
outcome: Risk of overall cancer and site-specific cancers (postmenopausal breast, colorectum, endometrium, thyroid, kidney, pancreas, liver, gallbladder, bladder, and stomach cancers)
population: General adult population from cohort studies
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies evaluates whether the risk of overall and site-specific cancers differs between individuals with different metabolic obesity phenotypes, specifically comparing metabolically unhealthy overweight/obese (MUOW/OB), metabolically unhealthy normal-weight (MUNW), and metabolically healthy overweight/obese (MHOW/OB) individuals to metabolically healthy normal-weight (MHNW) individuals.

comparison: Individuals who never used antibiotics (non-users)
exposure: Oral antibiotic use, including broad-spectrum and narrow-spectrum antibiotics, measured by ever-use and number of days exposed
outcome: Colorectal cancer risk (including colon cancer and rectal cancer separately)
population: General population, including individuals with and without antibiotic exposure (4.1 million individuals with over 73,550 colorectal cancer cases)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether oral antibiotic use is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer, examining whether this association varies between broad-spectrum and narrow-spectrum antibiotics, differs across the colorectal continuum (colon vs. rectal cancer), and whether a dose-response relationship exists based on duration of antibiotic exposure.

comparison: Non-carriers (general population without BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variants)
exposure: BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants
outcome: Prostate cancer risk (measured as relative risk)
population: Male BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants are associated with increased prostate cancer risk in male carriers compared to non-carriers, and explores how this risk varies by age, ethnicity, and variant location within the genes.

comparison: Progression-free survival, time-to-progression, or overall survival as reference clinical outcomes
exposure: Tumour response endpoints (overall response rate and complete response)
outcome: Strength of association (correlation and regression) between response-based endpoints and survival outcomes (OS, PFS, TTP)
population: Cancer patients across various cancer types, including non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and breast cancer
research_question: This systematic review of meta-analyses examines whether tumour response endpoints, such as overall response rate (ORR) and complete response (CR), are valid surrogate endpoints for progression-free survival (PFS), time-to-progression (TTP), or overall survival (OS) in cancer patients undergoing treatment.

comparison: Children with normal nutritional status or standard body composition
exposure: Nutritional status (undernutrition or overweight/obesity) and body composition
outcome: Pharmacokinetic parameters of antineoplastic drugs (mercaptopurine, vincristine, anthracyclines, methotrexate, busulfan, bevacizumab, and crizotinib) and appropriateness of dosing strategies
population: Children and adolescents with cancer (aged <21 years)
research_question: This systematic review examines how nutritional status (including undernutrition and overweight/obesity) and body composition affect the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of antineoplastic drugs, and whether current chemotherapy dosing strategies are appropriate for children and young people with cancer who have varying nutritional states.

comparison: No screening or uninformative comparison groups; younger age groups for some outcomes
exposure: Mammography screening
outcome: Breast cancer mortality, false positive tests, recall rates, biopsy rates, and overdiagnosis
population: Women aged 75 years and older
research_question: This systematic review examines the health benefits and harms of mammography screening in women aged 75 years and older, specifically evaluating the effects on breast cancer mortality, false positive rates, recall rates, and overdiagnosis compared to no screening or screening in younger age groups.

comparison: standard diagnostic methods/reference standard
exposure: HPV E6/E7 oncoprotein test
outcome: detection of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (sensitivity and specificity)
population: women undergoing cervical cancer screening, including HPV-positive women and HIV-positive women
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of HPV E6/E7 oncoprotein tests in detecting high-grade cervical lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse) compared to standard diagnostic methods in women undergoing cervical cancer screening.

comparison: pre-pandemic standard breast cancer care services
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic-related healthcare service disruptions and changes
outcome: changes in case detection rates, stage at diagnosis (stage shift), healthcare service organization, screening program delivery, treatment modalities (radiotherapy, surgery, endocrine therapy), and patient pathways
population: breast cancer patients in the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland
research_question: This scoping review examines how the COVID-19 pandemic affected breast cancer patient pathways and outcomes in the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, specifically investigating changes in diagnostic services, treatment approaches, screening programs, and clinical outcomes such as stage at diagnosis and case detection rates compared to pre-pandemic standard care.

comparison: Healthy control subjects without FSHD
exposure: FSHD disease status (presence of Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy)
outcome: Gene expression profiles and pathway dysregulation, including DUX4 biomarker expression, respiratory chain impairment, neuromuscular junction protein encoding genes, spliceosome regulation, and nuclear envelope protein expression alterations
population: FSHD patients and healthy control subjects (171 FSHD and 129 control samples from 13 omics datasets)
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to identify the molecular pathomechanisms and dysregulated pathways in Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) by comparing gene expression profiles from omics datasets of FSHD patients versus healthy controls, seeking to verify existing knowledge about DUX4 biomarkers and discover additional disease characteristics.

comparison: control groups (baseline or standard care)
intervention: culture-expanded mesenchymal stromal cell therapy
outcome: pain reduction, functional improvement, and cartilage protection/repair
population: patients with knee osteoarthritis
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether culture-expanded mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy improves pain, function, and cartilage preservation in patients with knee osteoarthritis compared to control treatments.

comparison: No comparison group (single-arm incidence study)
intervention: Docetaxel chemotherapy at licensed dose
outcome: Proportion of patients experiencing one or more episodes of febrile neutropenia (FN)
population: Patients with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving second-line chemotherapy
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to assess the incidence of febrile neutropenia in patients with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who are treated with docetaxel as second-line chemotherapy.

comparison: Pre-intervention state (no psychological intervention)
intervention: Psychological interventions (systematic desensitisation, hypnotherapy, and relaxation techniques)
outcome: Tolerance to dental treatments, absence of gagging, and adverse effects
population: Dental patients with sensitive gag reflex
research_question: This scoping review evaluates the effectiveness of psychological interventions, including systematic desensitisation, hypnotherapy, and relaxation techniques, in managing sensitive gag reflex among dental patients compared to their pre-intervention state, with outcomes measured by tolerance to dental treatments and absence of gagging.

comparison: White ethnic groups (white British, white Irish, and white other groups)
exposure: Ethnicity (minority ethnic group membership including Asian, Black, and other minority ethnic groups)
outcome: Oral health outcomes including caries levels, oral and pharyngeal cancer rates, tooth loss, edentulousness, self-rated oral health, and oral health behaviours/service utilization
population: Residents of the United Kingdom across all age groups, including children and adults from various ethnic groups
research_question: This scoping review aims to provide an overview and synthesis of the evidence on ethnic oral health inequalities in the United Kingdom, examining how oral health outcomes differ between minority ethnic groups and white ethnic groups across clinical, subjective, and oral health behaviour/service-related measures.

comparison: Traditional dental education settings (hospital or university-based dental clinics)
intervention: Community-based education (CBE) in dentistry, where dental students receive training and experience in community settings
outcome: Public health benefits including access to dental services (availability, affordability, acceptability, accessibility, accommodation), awareness and health literacy of students and communities, and clinical outcomes
population: Communities receiving dental services through community-based education programs and dental students participating in CBE
research_question: This scoping review examines what public health benefits are associated with community-based education (CBE) in dentistry, specifically investigating whether CBE improves access to dental services, health literacy, and clinical outcomes for communities compared to traditional dental education settings.

comparison: Various definitions, assessment tools (Dental Trust Scale, Dental Beliefs Survey, and other instruments), and professional perceptions across included studies
exposure: Dentist-patient trust relationship and its conceptualization in dental care settings
outcome: Definition of trust in dental context, measurement instruments for dentist-patient trust, and dental professionals' perceptions of patient trust (including the role of communication in building trusting relationships)
population: Dental patients and dental professionals (dentists and dental care providers)
research_question: This scoping review aims to explore how patient trust is defined and assessed in the dental literature, and how dental professionals perceive patient trust in the dentist-patient relationship.

comparison: Different ethical frameworks and approaches (biomedical ethics principles vs. public health ethics frameworks; individual-focused vs. population-focused ethical perspectives)
exposure: Community water fluoridation as a public health measure
outcome: Types of ethical frameworks applied, ethical arguments presented (collective benefit vs. autonomy/liberty concerns), and adequacy of ethical approaches for public health decision-making
population: Academic literature and studies discussing the ethics of community water fluoridation
research_question: This scoping review examines how the ethics of community water fluoridation has been appraised in the academic literature, exploring the ethical frameworks, principles, and approaches used to evaluate this public health intervention across different countries and perspectives.

comparison: Successful versus unsuccessful access to dental services; presence versus absence of barriers/facilitators
exposure: Barriers and facilitators to accessing oral healthcare services (including cost of services, perceptions of dentistry, availability of services, dental and social care workforce factors)
outcome: Access to oral healthcare services, including dental service utilization, availability of care, and factors affecting oral health maintenance
population: Older people aged 65 or older in the UK
research_question: This scoping review aims to identify the barriers and facilitators influencing older people's ability to access oral healthcare services in the UK, examining individual, organisational, and policy-level factors that affect dental service utilization among the elderly population.

comparison: Steroids alone
intervention: Topical tacrolimus (FK506) combined with steroids
outcome: Graft failure rates (measured as odds of graft failure)
population: Patients undergoing high-risk penetrating keratoplasty (HR-PKP), defined as those with previous keratoplasty, stromal neovascularisation affecting two or more corneal quadrants, and/or active inflammation or perforation at the time of surgery
research_question: This meta-analysis evaluates whether adjunctive topical tacrolimus combined with steroids reduces graft failure rates compared to steroids alone in patients undergoing high-risk penetrating keratoplasty.

comparison: Comparison across different clinical practice guidelines using AGREE II instrument assessment criteria
exposure: Clinical practice guideline recommendations for OCT and VA measurements in DMO management
outcome: Guideline quality scores (AGREE II domains), recommendations for OCT and VA use in initial diagnosis, initial disease management, disease monitoring, and anti-VEGF treatment response assessment
population: Adults with diabetic macular oedema (DMO)
research_question: This systematic review assesses the quality of global clinical practice guidelines for diabetic macular oedema management and evaluates the strength of recommendations for optical coherence tomography (OCT) and visual acuity (VA) measurements in diagnosis, initial management, and disease monitoring during anti-VEGF therapy.

comparison: Different training grades (foundation doctors versus more experienced Emergency Medicine physicians) and adequacy of formal ophthalmology training
exposure: Experience level and ophthalmology training received in Emergency Departments
outcome: Self-reported confidence in managing ophthalmic emergencies, confidence in performing funduscopy and using the slit lamp, and perceived adequacy of ophthalmology training
population: Doctors working in general Emergency Departments in the UK, including foundation doctors, Emergency Medicine trainees, specialty and associate specialist doctors, and EM consultants
research_question: This systematic review assesses the confidence of doctors working in general Emergency Departments in the UK in managing ophthalmic emergencies, including their confidence in performing funduscopy and using the slit lamp, and evaluates the adequacy of ophthalmology training received in the ED setting.

comparison: Standard surgical management, placebo, or no non-surgical intervention
intervention: Non-surgical interventions including corticosteroids, anti-VEGF therapies, heparin, anti-metabolites (5-fluorouracil, daunorubicin), and other pharmacological agents targeting inflammation, cell proliferation, and fibrosis pathways
outcome: Post-operative proliferative vitreoretinopathy incidence, retinal reattachment rate, and visual acuity
population: Patients with retinal detachment (rhegmatogenous retinal detachment or open globe injury-related retinal detachment) at risk of or with established proliferative vitreoretinopathy
research_question: This systematic review examines whether non-surgical interventions (including pharmacological agents such as corticosteroids, anti-VEGF therapies, heparin, and anti-metabolites like 5-fluorouracil and daunorubicin) can effectively prevent or treat proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) in patients with retinal detachment or ocular trauma compared to standard surgical management or placebo, as measured by post-operative PVR incidence, retinal reattachment rate, and visual acuity outcomes.

comparison: Healthy controls or non-mTBI subjects
exposure: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI)
outcome: Retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness measured by optical coherence tomography (OCT)
population: Adults with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI)
research_question: This systematic review examines whether adults with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) exhibit significant changes in retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness as measured by optical coherence tomography (OCT), compared to healthy controls, to assess the potential of OCT as a biomarker for visual system damage following mTBI.

comparison: Trade-offs between different attributes of glaucoma management (outcome attributes, process attributes, and cost attributes)
exposure: Stated-preference methodologies examining preferences for glaucoma treatment characteristics, health states, and services
outcome: Preferences and relative importance of glaucoma management attributes including treatment effectiveness, adverse events, affordability, recovery time, duration of effect, and monitoring burden
population: Glaucoma patients and healthcare professionals (ophthalmologists)
research_question: This systematic review aims to identify and critically appraise stated-preference studies that elicit preferences of glaucoma patients and healthcare professionals regarding different aspects of glaucoma management, including treatment options, health state valuations, and services, to determine which attributes are valued as most important.

comparison: Full ophthalmological examination or validated visual acuity measurement tools as gold standard reference tests
exposure: Home-based screening tools for amblyopia (internet-based tools, smartphone/tablet applications, digital cameras, home-based questionnaires and visual acuity tools)
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy expressed as sensitivity and specificity for amblyopia detection
population: Children aged less than 1 month to 16 years old
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and reliability of home-based screening tools for detecting amblyopia in children compared to gold standard ophthalmological examination or validated visual acuity measurement tools.

comparison: Comparison between different gene-based therapies (onasemnogene abeparvovec vs risdiplam vs nusinersen) and pre-treatment baseline status
intervention: Gene-based therapies including onasemnogene abeparvovec, risdiplam, and nusinersen
outcome: Survival rate, need for ventilatory support, motor function improvement (CHOP-INTEND score ≥4 points), and adverse drug reactions (headaches, vomiting, gastrointestinal disorders)
population: Patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) types 1 and 2
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the effects of gene-based therapies (onasemnogene abeparvovec, risdiplam, and nusinersen) on patient survival, need for ventilatory support, motor function improvement, and incidence of adverse drug reactions in patients with spinal muscular atrophy types 1 and 2.

comparison: No job strain or low job strain
exposure: Job strain (work-related psychosocial stress)
outcome: Weight gain, obesity development, and body mass index changes
population: Working adults
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether job strain (work-related psychosocial stress) is associated with increased risk of weight gain and obesity development in working adults compared to those without job strain, and whether reduction in job strain over time is associated with lower obesity risk.

comparison: Non-yoghurt consumers or lower yoghurt consumption levels
exposure: Yoghurt consumption
outcome: Weight-related outcomes including body mass index, body weight/weight gain, waist circumference, and body fat
population: Apparently healthy adults
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether yoghurt consumption is associated with weight-related outcomes, including body weight, body mass index, waist circumference, and body fat, in apparently healthy adults compared to non-consumers or lower consumption levels.

comparison: Comparison between indoor versus outdoor air exposure, active versus passive sampling methods, different age groups, and environmental samples versus toxicology study doses
exposure: Inhalation exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics in indoor and outdoor air
outcome: Calculated inhalation exposure doses of microplastics across different age groups and environments, identification of data gaps for quantifying human inhalation exposures
population: General human population across different age groups including infants, preschool children, middle-school aged children, adolescents, pregnant women, and non-pregnant adults
research_question: This systematic review aims to quantify human inhalation exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics from indoor and outdoor air across different age groups, and to identify critical data gaps and establish a framework for assessing health risks associated with airborne microplastic exposure.

comparison: Venipuncture-based blood sampling methods (gold standard) and plasma/serum sample analysis
exposure: Environmental toxicants including environmental tobacco smoke, trace elements (lead, mercury, cadmium, arsenic), and industrial chemicals (endocrine-disrupting chemicals and persistent organic pollutants)
outcome: Analytical method performance parameters including analytical sensitivity, specificity, sample volume requirements, contamination considerations, extracted blood volume estimation, biomarker stability, analyte recovery, and hematocrit effects
population: Human subjects, with particular focus on newborns, infants, and children in population-based and field-based epidemiological studies
research_question: This systematic review examines the current state of analytical methods for measuring environmental exposure biomarkers (including environmental tobacco smoke, trace elements, and industrial chemicals) in dried blood spot samples, evaluating method development, validation, and application studies to guide researchers in using DBS sampling for public health and epidemiological research.

comparison: Placebo or active drug control without MRA addition
intervention: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) such as spironolactone or eplerenone as add-on therapy to RAS inhibitors
outcome: Office systolic and diastolic blood pressure reduction, serum potassium levels, and albuminuria
population: Patients with hypertension and diabetes mellitus already receiving renin-angiotensin system inhibitor therapy
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the antihypertensive effects and safety of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) as add-on therapy to renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors in patients with both hypertension and diabetes mellitus, specifically examining blood pressure reduction and the risk of hyperkalemia.

comparison: Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) therapy
intervention: Chlorthalidone (CTLD) therapy
outcome: Blood pressure control (systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure changes), safety profile (serum potassium and serum sodium levels)
population: Patients with hypertension
research_question: This meta-analysis compares the efficacy and safety of chlorthalidone versus hydrochlorothiazide in patients with hypertension, specifically examining their effects on blood pressure control (systolic and diastolic blood pressure) and safety profiles including electrolyte balance.

comparison: Oral antipsychotics
intervention: Long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics
outcome: All-cause mortality, suicidal mortality, and non-suicidal mortality
population: Patients with schizophrenia, including those with first-episode psychosis and chronic schizophrenia
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether patients with schizophrenia receiving long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics have lower all-cause, suicidal, and non-suicidal mortality compared to those receiving oral antipsychotics. It also examines whether this mortality difference is moderated by factors such as antipsychotic drug type, age, sex, race, sample type (first-episode psychosis vs chronic schizophrenia), study design, follow-up length, industry sponsorship, and study quality.

comparison: varying levels of genetic versus environmental influences
exposure: genetic and environmental factors
outcome: childhood victimization (including maltreatment and bullying)
population: children and adolescents from twin studies
research_question: This meta-analysis examines the relative contributions of genetic and environmental influences on childhood victimization based on twin studies, and investigates whether these influences vary depending on the reporter of victimization, type of victimization, and age at exposure.

comparison: alcohol-naïve controls
exposure: chronic alcohol consumption/alcohol use disorder
outcome: differentially expressed genes and transcriptomic signatures in brain regions (prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, amygdala)
population: patients with alcohol use disorder and animal models (mice, rats, monkeys) with chronic alcohol exposure
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the transcriptomic signatures and differentially expressed genes in brain tissue from patients with alcohol use disorder and animal models of chronic alcohol exposure compared to alcohol-naïve controls, aiming to identify conserved molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets across species.

comparison: Individuals who do not meet CHR-P criteria (CHR-P-)
exposure: CHR-P status as determined by psychometric instruments (CAARMS, SIPS, BSABS, SPI-A, SPI-CY) or diagnostic criteria (DSM-5 Attenuated Psychosis Syndrome)
