outcome: Prognostic accuracy for transition to psychotic disorders, indexed by area-under-the-curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and Population Attributable Fraction (PAF)
population: Individuals at clinical high-risk for psychosis (CHR-P), aged 12-40 years, referred to CHR-P services or diagnosed with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to determine the prognostic accuracy and clinical utility of psychometric instruments (such as CAARMS, SIPS, and Basic Symptom assessments) in predicting transition to psychotic disorders among individuals at clinical high-risk for psychosis (CHR-P), comparing those who meet CHR-P criteria (CHR-P+) with those who do not (CHR-P-).

comparison: Healthy controls without depression
exposure: Depression diagnosis
outcome: Absolute counts and relative percentages of flow cytometry-derived white blood cell subsets (including total WBC, granulocytes, neutrophils, monocytes, CD4+ helper T cells, CD8+ T cells, natural killer cells, B cells, activated T cells, Th1 cells, Th2 cells, and total lymphocytes)
population: Individuals with depression
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether individuals with depression exhibit alterations in peripheral blood white blood cell subsets (including granulocytes, neutrophils, monocytes, T cells, B cells, and natural killer cells) measured by flow cytometry compared to healthy controls, to characterize the cellular immunophenotype associated with depression.

comparison: Control interventions including needs-based care
intervention: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), family-focused therapy, Integrated Psychological Therapy, antipsychotics, omega-3 fatty acids, CBT plus risperidone, minocycline, and other non-pharmacological approaches (cognitive remediation, sleep-targeted therapy, brain stimulation)
outcome: Transition to psychosis (primary outcome), symptoms severity, and functioning
population: Individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether preventive interventions, including cognitive behavioral therapy, family-focused therapy, antipsychotics, omega-3 fatty acids, and other pharmacological and non-pharmacological approaches, can reduce the risk of transition to psychosis and improve symptoms severity and functioning in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P) compared to control interventions or needs-based care.

comparison: Placebo
intervention: Perioperative intravenous administration of ketamine
outcome: Postoperative depression scores, postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, and adverse effects (nausea and vomiting, headache, hallucination, dizziness)
population: Patients undergoing surgery
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether perioperative intravenous administration of ketamine reduces postoperative depression scores and pain in patients undergoing surgery compared to placebo, and evaluates the associated adverse effects.

comparison: Pregnant people with mental disorders not receiving psychotropic medications (controlling for confounding by indication)
exposure: Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy (including antidepressants, SSRIs, and paroxetine)
outcome: Adverse health outcomes including preterm birth, small for gestational age, major congenital malformations, and cardiac malformations
population: Pregnant people with mental disorders (including depression and anxiety)
research_question: This umbrella review aims to quantify the strength of associations between psychotropic medication use during pregnancy in people with mental disorders and various adverse health outcomes in both pregnant people and foetuses, while controlling for underlying maternal psychiatric conditions (confounding by indication).

comparison: Chromosomally normal individuals without Down syndrome
intervention: Professional tooth cleaning combined with oral hygiene reinforcement/instructions
outcome: Reduction in periodontal probing pocket depth (PPD)
population: Individuals diagnosed with Down syndrome
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the effectiveness of periodontal prevention and treatment modalities in individuals diagnosed with Down syndrome compared to chromosomally normal individuals, specifically examining whether professional tooth cleaning combined with oral hygiene reinforcement reduces periodontal probing pocket depth.

comparison: Low-dose vitamin D supplementation (<800 IU/day)
intervention: High-dose vitamin D supplementation (≥800 IU/day)
outcome: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, growth velocities, vitamin D deficiency, skeletal hypomineralization, mortality, vitamin D excess, and neurodevelopmental outcomes
population: Preterm infants
research_question: This meta-analysis evaluates the short-term and long-term effectiveness and safety of high-dose (≥800 IU/day) versus low-dose (<800 IU/day) vitamin D supplementation in preterm infants, examining outcomes including serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, growth velocities, vitamin D deficiency, skeletal hypomineralization, mortality, and neurodevelopmental outcomes.

comparison: Placebo and delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) as positive control
intervention: Acute cannabidiol (CBD) administration
outcome: Cognitive and psychomotor performance measures including objective performance tasks and subjective measures such as self-reported sedation
population: Adults participating in controlled human laboratory studies
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether acute cannabidiol (CBD) use impairs cognitive and psychomotor performance in adults compared to placebo, and further compares the magnitude of any impairment effects to those produced by delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) as a positive control.

comparison: Daytime (diurnal) insect activity levels
exposure: Diel period (nocturnal vs. diurnal activity periods)
outcome: Insect abundance and taxonomic richness differences between day and night periods
population: Insect communities worldwide across various ecosystems (aquatic and terrestrial)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether insect communities exhibit higher activity levels during nocturnal periods compared to diurnal periods at a global scale, and examines how environmental factors such as habitat type (aquatic vs. terrestrial), temperature, and latitude moderate diel variation in insect abundance and taxonomic richness.

comparison: Control conditions (including non-intervention control groups in randomised and non-randomised controlled studies)
intervention: Group arts interventions (shared artistic experiences such as dance, painting, and other art forms)
outcome: Depression and anxiety symptom levels
population: Older adults aged over 55 years without dementia
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether group arts interventions, where individuals engage together in shared artistic experiences such as dance or painting, are effective in reducing depression and anxiety symptoms among older adults (aged over 55 years without dementia) compared to control conditions.

comparison: Comparisons across demographic groups (e.g., younger vs. older age groups, women vs. men, different geographic regions, varying levels of media exposure and perceived government action)
exposure: Social factors (age, developmental stage, gender, ethnicity, media exposure, socioeconomic context, intergenerational relations, peer and cultural norms), political factors (distrust, government inaction, individual views and participation), and geographic factors (exposure to environmental hazards, cross-country differences, urban-rural residence)
outcome: Eco-anxiety levels, including climate anxiety, climate worry, and related psychological distress measures assessed through instruments such as the Climate Change Anxiety Scale (CCAS) and Hogg Eco-Anxiety Scale (HEAS)
population: Children and young people (CYP), including adolescents and young adults
research_question: This systematic review examines the social, political, and geographic factors associated with eco-anxiety (psychological distress arising from climate and environmental changes) among children and young people, exploring how factors such as age, gender, media exposure, government inaction, and geographic location influence the development and expression of eco-anxiety in younger populations.

comparison: Individuals with low symptom burden after concussion
exposure: Concussion with persisting symptoms (high symptom burden versus low symptom burden)
outcome: Neural network dysfunction patterns identified through fMRI, specifically salience network connectivity and localization of cortical regions suitable for neuromodulation targeting
population: Individuals with persisting symptoms after concussion (PSaC), characterized by physical, cognitive and emotional symptoms persisting for at least 4 weeks beyond the acute phase of injury
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to identify a core neural network associated with persisting symptoms after concussion (PSaC) using multimodal neuroimaging approaches, and to explore whether differences in network disruption are evident between individuals with high versus low symptom burden, with the goal of identifying candidate cortical targets for neuromodulation therapy.

comparison: Healthy control individuals
exposure: Eating disorder diagnosis (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder)
outcome: Peripheral cytokine concentrations (IL-6, IL-15, IL-7, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-4, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, MCP, TGF-β)
population: People diagnosed with eating disorders (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and other specified feeding and eating disorders)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether cytokine concentrations differ between people diagnosed with eating disorders (including anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge eating disorder) and healthy controls, and examines how cytokine levels change longitudinally during weight restoration in individuals with anorexia nervosa.

comparison: Patients without the respective risk factors (e.g., male sex, younger age, non-smokers, non-diabetics, non-STEMI)
exposure: Risk factors including female sex, advanced age, smoking, diabetes, and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
outcome: Incidence of cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, and 1-year mortality
population: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the risk factors associated with the incidence of cardiogenic shock following acute myocardial infarction (AMI-CS) and its poor outcomes, including in-hospital death, 30-day mortality, and 1-year mortality, comparing patients with these risk factors to those without.

comparison: Traditional healthcare information sources and standard patient care without LLM assistance
exposure: Use of large language models (primarily GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) for patient care applications including answering medical questions, patient information generation, medical text summarization, translation, and clinical documentation
outcome: LLM applications in patient care (answering medical questions, patient information generation, clinical documentation) and limitations (design limitations including lack of medical domain optimization, data transparency, accessibility issues; output limitations including non-reproducibility, non-comprehensiveness, incorrectness, unsafety, and bias)
population: Patients and caregivers using large language models for disease management and healthcare support
research_question: This systematic review aims to synthesize and analyze the current applications and limitations of large language models (LLMs) in patient care, examining how LLMs are being used by patients or caregivers for disease management, medical education, and health information access compared to traditional healthcare information sources.

comparison: Reference exposure level of 2.0 µg/m³ PM2.5 (theoretical minimum exposure level)
exposure: Long-term ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure
outcome: Dementia outcomes including all-cause dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and vascular dementia incidence and risk
population: General population, particularly individuals aged 75 years and older at risk for dementia
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the association between long-term ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure and dementia outcomes, including all-cause dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and vascular dementia, using the Burden of Proof meta-analytic framework to characterize the dose-response relationship and quantify the strength of evidence.

comparison: Individuals without depression (healthy controls)
exposure: Depression status (presence of depressive disorder)
outcome: Blood and cerebrospinal fluid chemokine concentrations (including CCL2, CCL3, CCL4, CCL5, CCL7, CCL11, CXCL4, CXCL7, CXCL8, CXCL9, CXCL10)
population: Individuals with depression, including both physically healthy participants and those with physical/inflammatory illness
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether blood or cerebrospinal fluid chemokine concentrations differ between individuals with depression and those without depression, and whether these differences are observed in physically healthy individuals versus those with inflammatory illness.

comparison: Healthy controls without ADHD, or methylphenidate non-responders for pharmacogenetic studies
exposure: Genetic variants (candidate genes including BAIAP2, SLC6A3, DRD4, COMT), pharmacogenetic markers related to methylphenidate response, and biochemical markers (cortisol, polyunsaturated fatty acids including DHA)
outcome: Association with adult ADHD diagnosis (genetic and biochemical studies) and response to methylphenidate treatment (pharmacogenetic studies), measured through effect sizes of genetic polymorphisms and levels of peripheral biomarkers such as salivary cortisol and serum docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)
population: Adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to identify potential genetic markers (from candidate gene association studies), pharmacogenetic predictors of methylphenidate response, and peripheral biochemical/metabolomic markers that are specifically associated with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults, compared to healthy controls or non-responders.

comparison: Seizure onset >12 months as reference group; comparisons across different mutation types and variant locations
exposure: Age at seizure onset (≤12 months vs >12 months), mutation type, variant location, and mode of inheritance
outcome: Severity of intellectual disability, psychiatric comorbidities (including hyperactive, autistic, and obsessive-compulsive features), and genotype-phenotype associations
population: Individuals with PCDH19 gene variants, including affected females, mosaic males, and hemizygous males with PCDH19-associated epilepsy (EFMR/PCDH19-GCE)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis characterizes the neuropsychiatric profile of PCDH19-associated epilepsy (EFMR) and examines whether clinical and molecular factors, including age at seizure onset, mutation type, variant location, and mode of inheritance, are associated with cognitive function and psychiatric comorbidities in affected individuals.

comparison: Healthy controls
exposure: First-episode psychosis as a multisystem disorder affecting CNS and non-CNS organ systems
outcome: Effect sizes for CNS alterations (brain structure, neurophysiology, neurochemistry) and non-CNS alterations (immune parameters, cardiometabolic parameters, HPA axis parameters), and correlations between non-CNS alterations, CNS changes, and psychopathological symptoms
population: People with first-episode psychosis (FEP)
research_question: This meta-review examines whether people with first-episode psychosis show alterations in non-CNS systems (immune, cardiometabolic, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal systems) compared to healthy controls, how these alterations compare in magnitude to CNS abnormalities (brain structural, neurophysiological, and neurochemical parameters), and whether non-CNS alterations correlate with CNS changes and psychopathological symptoms.

comparison: Standard blood pressure management or control groups with systolic blood pressure ≥130 mmHg
intervention: Strict blood pressure control achieving systolic blood pressure <130 mmHg (using mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, intensive BP control, or intensive HF management)
outcome: Heart failure hospitalizations, all-cause mortality, hypotension, renal dysfunction, and serious adverse events
population: Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether managing systolic blood pressure to below 130 mmHg improves clinical outcomes, including heart failure hospitalizations and all-cause mortality, in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) compared to standard blood pressure management.

comparison: Controlled hypertension (CH), white coat uncontrolled resistant hypertension (WCURH), and ambulatory nonresistant hypertension (ANRH)
exposure: Ambulatory resistant hypertension (ARH), defined as 24-hour blood pressure ≥130/80 mmHg during treatment with ≥3 antihypertensive drugs
outcome: Heart failure incidence (hazard ratio for heart failure events)
population: Treated hypertensive patients with different ambulatory blood pressure phenotypes
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether ambulatory resistant hypertension (ARH) is associated with an increased risk of developing heart failure compared to other ambulatory blood pressure phenotypes, including controlled hypertension, white coat uncontrolled resistant hypertension, and ambulatory nonresistant hypertension, in treated hypertensive patients.

comparison: Neonates with mother-neonate separation vs. those without separation; breastfed neonates vs. non-breastfed neonates
exposure: Mother-neonate separation from birth and breastfeeding practices
outcome: Transmission route classification (vertical vs. environmental), COVID-19 development rate, clinical manifestations (fever, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and neurological symptoms), lung imaging abnormalities, and late-onset SARS-CoV-2 infection incidence
population: Neonates (infants in the first month of life) with SARS-CoV-2 infection confirmed by positive nasopharyngeal swab and/or specific IgM
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to clarify the transmission routes (vertical vs. environmental), clinical features, and outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infections in neonates, and to examine whether mother-neonate separation from birth and breastfeeding are associated with the incidence of late-onset neonatal SARS-CoV-2 infections.

comparison: Control conditions without active intrusion modulation techniques
intervention: Experimental techniques including behavioral interventions (imagery-based such as Tetris, verbal-conceptual, emotional processing), pharmacological interventions (e.g., oxytocin, alcohol), and neuromodulation techniques (transcranial electrical/magnetic stimulation)
outcome: Intrusive memory frequency (measured via daily diaries, lab tasks, or self-report questionnaires), intrusion-related emotional distress, and post-traumatic symptoms (e.g., sleep difficulties, emotional reactions, hyperarousal)
population: Non-clinical populations exposed to lab-analogue trauma (healthy adults without clinical PTSD)
research_question: This meta-analysis examines whether experimental techniques (behavioral, pharmacological, and neuromodulation interventions) can effectively modulate intrusive memory frequency, intrusion-related distress, and post-traumatic symptoms following lab-analogue trauma exposure in non-clinical populations, and investigates which categories of techniques are most effective and at what timing of administration.

comparison: Unvaccinated pregnant people
intervention: COVID-19 vaccination (predominantly mRNA vaccines)
outcome: Vaccine effectiveness against RT-PCR confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, stillbirth, miscarriage, gestational age at birth, placental abruption, pulmonary embolism, postpartum haemorrhage, maternal death, intensive care unit admission, birthweight Z-score, and neonatal intensive care unit admission
population: Pregnant people (117,552 COVID-19 vaccinated pregnant individuals across 23 studies)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination (primarily mRNA vaccines) against SARS-CoV-2 infection in pregnant people and examines whether vaccination is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes including stillbirth, miscarriage, preterm birth, and other maternal and neonatal complications compared to unvaccinated pregnant individuals.

comparison: Different acclimation temperatures (baseline or lower/higher acclimation conditions)
exposure: Thermal acclimation (changes in acclimation temperature)
outcome: Critical thermal limits measured as acclimation response ratio (ARR) - change in critical thermal maximum (CTmax) and critical thermal minimum (CTmin) per degree change in acclimation temperature
population: Insects across 102 species including pollinators, pests, and disease vectors
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the extent to which insects can adjust their critical thermal limits (CTmax and CTmin) through thermal acclimation plasticity, and examines how factors such as latitude, habitat type, sex, body size, life stage, and development type influence this plasticity in response to climate change.

comparison: Unvaccinated pre-Omicron convalescent plasma donors and two-dose mRNA vaccinated non-convalescent individuals
exposure: Vaccination status and prior SARS-CoV-2 infection history (unvaccinated convalescent, vaccinated non-convalescent, vaccinated convalescent/hybrid immunity)
outcome: Omicron-neutralizing antibody titers measured as geometric mean of geometric mean titers for 50% neutralization (GM(GMT50)) and percentage of plasma samples neutralizing Omicron variants (BA.1, BA.2, BA.4/5)
population: COVID-19 convalescent plasma donors and vaccinated individuals, including unvaccinated pre-Omicron convalescents, vaccinated non-convalescents, and vaccinated convalescents
research_question: This systematic review examines the Omicron-neutralizing antibody titers in different COVID-19 convalescent plasma sources, comparing plasma from unvaccinated pre-Omicron donors, vaccinated non-convalescent individuals, and vaccinated convalescents (Vax-CCP) to determine which plasma sources provide effective neutralization against Omicron variants (BA.1, BA.2, BA.4/5).

comparison: Unvaccinated individuals or primary course vaccination only (for booster comparisons)
exposure: COVID-19 vaccination status (any dose, primary course vaccination, or booster vaccination)
outcome: Risk of developing long COVID (odds ratio of long COVID occurrence)
population: Individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2, particularly Omicron variants
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates whether COVID-19 vaccination, including primary course and booster vaccination, reduces the risk of developing long COVID in individuals subsequently infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants compared to unvaccinated individuals or those with fewer vaccine doses.

comparison: Pathological assessment of surgical resection specimen (reference standard for pathological complete remission)
exposure: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, stratified by immunohistochemistry-based molecular subtypes (HR−/HER2−, HR−/HER2+, HR+/HER2−, HR+/HER2+) and MRI field strength (1.5T vs 3.0T)
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy measures including sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) for predicting pathological complete remission (pCR)
population: Patients with early-stage breast cancer receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to estimate and compare the diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value) of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting pathological complete remission (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with early-stage breast cancer, stratified by molecular subtype based on immunohistochemistry (HR and HER2 status), and to explore the impact of other factors such as MRI field strength on accuracy.

comparison: Lower adherence to the Mediterranean diet
exposure: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet
outcome: Cancer incidence and cancer mortality
population: Older adults
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether higher adherence to the Mediterranean diet is associated with reduced cancer incidence and lower cancer-related mortality in older adults compared to those with lower adherence to the Mediterranean diet.

comparison: Medical treatment alone and septuagenarians (patients aged 70-79 years) undergoing surgical repair
intervention: Surgical repair for Type A aortic dissection
outcome: Surgical outcomes including re-exploration rates, stroke, respiratory failure, antegrade cerebral perfusion, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, myocardial ischemic time, tracheostomy, neurologic complications, and renal failure
population: Octogenarians (patients aged 80 years and older) with Type A aortic dissection
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the long-term surgical outcomes of Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) repair in octogenarians, examining whether surgical intervention achieves favorable outcomes compared to medical treatment, and how outcomes in octogenarians compare to septuagenarians, with a focus on factors including surgical approach, comorbidities, and preoperative status.

comparison: Acetogenic versus methanogenic MES cells; biofilm versus planktonic communities; different inoculum pre-treatment conditions
exposure: Inoculum pre-treatment methods (heat shock, BESA chemical treatment) and operating parameters (pH, temperature, cathode potential)
outcome: Core microbiome composition, microbial community structure, relative abundance of key taxa (Desulfovibrio, Acetobacterium, Methanobacterium), community assembly patterns, and cell performance indicators
population: Microbial communities (biofilm and planktonic) in microbial electrosynthesis cells from 22 studies using various inocula including anaerobic and activated sludges
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the composition and dynamics of microbial communities (biofilm and planktonic) in microbial electrosynthesis (MES) cells, examining how different inoculum pre-treatments and operating parameters affect the core microbiome structure and the balance between acetogenic and methanogenic pathways in CO2 bioelectrocatalytic conversion systems.

comparison: Patients with visceral metastases (including liver and non-liver visceral metastases) versus patients with non-visceral metastases only
intervention: Endocrine monotherapies including fulvestrant (SERD), tamoxifen (SERM), and aromatase inhibitors (anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane) in first- and second-line treatment settings
outcome: Progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), clinical benefit rate (CBR), and duration of clinical benefit (DoCB)
population: Postmenopausal patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with metastatic disease
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether endocrine monotherapies (including fulvestrant, tamoxifen, and aromatase inhibitors) are more efficacious in patients with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer whose disease involves non-visceral metastases compared to those with visceral metastases, and whether clinical outcomes differ between patients with liver versus non-liver visceral metastases.

comparison: Moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) at 60-70% maximal heart rate
intervention: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) at 85-95% maximal heart rate
outcome: Vascular function measures including flow-mediated dilation (FMD), arterial diameter, arterial stiffness, pulse wave velocity, and blood flow
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with overweight or obesity (BMI 25-36 kg/m²)
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether high-intensity interval training (HIIT) is more effective than moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) in improving vascular function, including flow-mediated dilation, arterial diameter, arterial stiffness, pulse wave velocity, and blood flow, among adults with overweight and obesity.

comparison: Daily long-acting or ultra-long-acting insulin (insulin glargine and insulin degludec)
intervention: Once-weekly tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, and 15 mg doses)
outcome: HbA1c, 2-hour postprandial blood sugar, pre-meal blood sugar, body weight, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, lipid profiles (total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, VLDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol), and risk of hypoglycemia
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates whether once-weekly tirzepatide is more effective and safer than long-acting or ultra-long-acting insulin (insulin glargine and degludec) in managing type 2 diabetes, with outcomes including glycemic control (HbA1c), blood sugar levels, body weight, blood pressure, lipid profiles, and risk of hypoglycemia.

comparison: Advantaged socioeconomic position (higher SEP groups)
exposure: Socioeconomic position (SEP), including measures such as parental education, income, and other socioeconomic indicators
outcome: Body composition measures including fat mass (FM), fat-free mass (FFM), lean mass (LM), fat mass index (FMI), and fat distribution (central adiposity, android-to-gynoid fat mass ratio)
population: Children and adolescents up to and including 18 years from general population samples in high-income and middle-income countries
research_question: This systematic review examines the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) and body composition measures (fat mass, fat-free mass, and fat distribution) in children and adolescents up to 18 years of age, comparing those from disadvantaged versus advantaged socioeconomic backgrounds across high-income and middle-income countries.

comparison: Different levels or patterns of dietary intake within the bariatric surgery population
exposure: Post-surgery dietary intake including macronutrient composition, food group patterns, and diet quality
outcome: Weight outcomes including weight loss and weight recurrence at 12 months or longer post-surgery
population: Adults who have undergone bariatric surgery
research_question: This systematic review examines whether post-surgery dietary intake, including macronutrient composition (carbohydrate, protein, fat), food group patterns, and diet quality, is associated with weight outcomes (weight loss and weight recurrence) in adults who have undergone bariatric surgery at 12 months or longer after the procedure.

comparison: Traditional data sources used in obesity research
exposure: Obesogenic environmental factors studied through non-traditional data sources (geospatial data/GIS, social networks, digital devices)
outcome: Identification and characterization of non-traditional data sources, their applications across obesogenic environment domains (physical, sociocultural, political, economic), and obesity-related outcomes
population: Adults in obesity research studies
research_question: This systematic review aims to identify and characterize the different sources of non-traditional data (such as geospatial data, social networks, and digital devices) and their applications in studying obesogenic environments across physical, sociocultural, political, and economic domains in adult obesity research.

comparison: Parent-child interventions, minimal contact interventions, and waiting list controls
intervention: Group-based, parent-only weight management interventions without individual component
outcome: Children's weight status (BMI, weight for height), health behaviors (diet, physical activity, sedentary behavior), psychological wellbeing (self-esteem, self-efficacy), and factors associated with treatment outcomes (session attendance, child's age and baseline weight, socioeconomic status, home food environment modifications)
population: Children and adolescents of all weight status (including those who are overweight, obese, or at risk of developing overweight) and their parents
research_question: This systematic review assesses the effectiveness of group-based, parent-only interventions (without child participation) on children's weight status, health behaviors, and psychological wellbeing across all weight categories, and identifies socio-demographic characteristics, process indicators, and contextual factors that contribute to successful intervention outcomes.

comparison: Outpatient weight loss treatment phase
intervention: Inpatient hospitalized multidisciplinary weight loss programs (with short-term follow-up of max 6 months or long-term follow-up up to 24 months)
outcome: Body weight change and body mass index (BMI) change
population: Obese patients undergoing weight loss treatment programs
research_question: This meta-analysis aims to compare the effects of inpatient treatment (hospitalized weight loss programs) versus outpatient treatment on body weight and BMI changes in obese patients, and to determine whether short-term (up to 6 months follow-up) or long-term (up to 24 months follow-up) hospitalization shows better outcomes for weight loss.

comparison: Physicians (overall, expert physicians, and non-expert physicians)
exposure: Diagnostic assessment using generative AI models
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and diagnostic performance
population: Medical diagnostic cases/clinical scenarios used to validate generative AI diagnostic capabilities
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic performance of generative artificial intelligence models in medical diagnostics and compares their diagnostic accuracy with that of physicians, including both expert and non-expert clinicians.

comparison: Standard care, usual care, or no digital intervention (control groups)
intervention: Digital interventions including client education (website, social media, texting), client reminders (SMS, email), client education plus reminders, provider education (webinar, email), and provider reminders (electronic medical records, texting)
outcome: HPV vaccination uptake (HVU)
population: Individuals eligible for HPV vaccination, including adolescents, young adults, and mixed-gender populations
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the efficacy of digital interventions, comparing educational approaches (client education, provider education) and reminder approaches (client reminders, provider reminders, and combined client education plus reminders), for promoting HPV vaccination uptake among individuals eligible for HPV vaccination compared to standard care or no intervention.

comparison: Standard inpatient care, treatment as usual, or control conditions without EMH components
intervention: E-mental health (EMH) interventions including app-based, web-based, text message, video, or digital monitoring delivered as blended interventions or post-treatment aftercare
outcome: Mental health outcomes including symptom reduction and treatment efficacy, with assessment of long-term stability at follow-up
population: Patients with mental health disorders in inpatient settings
research_question: This meta-analysis investigates the efficacy of e-mental health (EMH) interventions, including blended interventions and post-treatment aftercare, on mental health outcomes in patients receiving inpatient psychiatric treatment compared to standard care or control conditions.

comparison: In-person clinical assessment (face-to-face examination as reference standard)
exposure: Telemedicine assessment methods (photograph-based and video-based remote consultations)
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy measures including sensitivity and specificity for surgical site infection detection
population: Postoperative surgical patients (mean age 47.1 ± 13.3 years)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of telemedicine (including photograph and video-based methods) for detecting surgical site infections in postoperative patients compared to in-person clinical assessment as the reference standard.

comparison: Normal controls and patients with atypical parkinsonism
exposure: Artificial intelligence (machine learning and deep learning) algorithms applied to PET imaging (presynaptic dopamine, postsynaptic dopamine, and 18F-FDG tracers)
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy measured by area under the curve (AUC) derived from binary diagnostic accuracy data (sensitivity and specificity)
population: Patients with Parkinson's disease, normal controls, and patients with atypical parkinsonism (including multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence-assisted PET imaging for detecting Parkinson's disease, comparing AI algorithm performance across different PET tracers (presynaptic dopamine, postsynaptic dopamine, and 18F-FDG) in distinguishing PD patients from normal controls and from patients with atypical parkinsonism.

comparison: Different AI algorithms and different types of wearable devices; traditional depression assessment methods (clinical observations, self-reported questionnaires such as PHQ-9)
exposure: Use of wearable artificial intelligence systems (wearable devices paired with AI algorithms) for analyzing biomarkers and biosignals such as heart rates, physical activities, sleep patterns, and blood oxygen
outcome: Diagnostic and predictive performance metrics including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and root mean square error (RMSE)
population: Individuals with depression or at risk of depression (general population across all age groups)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the performance of wearable artificial intelligence (AI) systems in detecting and predicting depression among individuals, evaluating metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and root mean square error across different algorithms and wearable devices.

comparison: Other psychiatric disorders, trauma-exposed controls, healthy controls; single data types versus multi-dimensional data
exposure: Machine learning algorithms applied to various data types (text, scales, brain images, behavioral and physiological indicators, multi-dimensional data)
outcome: Classification accuracy of PTSD identification (overall accuracy 0.89; multi-dimensional data accuracy 0.96; single data types accuracy 0.86-0.90)
population: Individuals with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), trauma-exposed individuals, and healthy controls
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the accuracy of machine learning techniques in classifying and identifying individuals with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to other psychiatric disorders, trauma-exposed controls, or healthy controls, and evaluates whether multi-dimensional data types yield better classification performance than single data types.

comparison: Control conditions (apps with fewer or no engagement features, waitlist controls, or other comparison conditions in randomized controlled trials)
intervention: Standalone smartphone apps for depression and/or anxiety incorporating persuasive system design features and behavioral economics techniques
outcome: Symptoms of depression and anxiety, user engagement measures (completion rate, retention)
population: Symptomatic participants with depression and/or anxiety symptoms
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether smartphone apps for depression and anxiety are efficacious in reducing symptoms, and investigates which persuasive system design (PSD) features and behavioral economics techniques increase sustained user engagement and whether the number of engagement features is associated with greater clinical efficacy.

comparison: Non-CBT control conditions
intervention: Internet-based and mobile-based cognitive behavioral therapy (IM-CBT)
outcome: Primary outcomes: psychiatric symptoms (depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, PTSD symptoms, general psychological distress) from baseline to post-intervention and follow-ups; Secondary outcomes: physical distress (physical symptoms, functional impairment, self-rated ill health, objective physiological dysfunction)
population: Patients with chronic diseases (including chronic pain, cancer, arthritis, cardiovascular disease, and other chronic medical conditions)
research_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether internet-based and mobile-based cognitive behavioral therapy (IM-CBT) is effective in reducing psychiatric symptoms (depressive, anxiety, PTSD symptoms, general psychological distress) and physical distress (physical symptoms, functional impairment, self-rated ill health, objective physiological dysfunction) among patients with chronic diseases compared to non-CBT control conditions. The study also investigates the active therapeutic components responsible for clinical improvements, effect moderators, and the reciprocal relationship between mental health and physical health outcomes.

comparison: Standard care or usual care pathways without mobile device-based active remote monitoring
intervention: Mobile device-based active remote monitoring technologies requiring frequent patient-reported responses via smartphone or tablet applications
outcome: Cost-effectiveness (incremental costs and health outcomes including quality-adjusted life years, prevention of condition worsening, and healthcare resource utilization)
population: People with long-term conditions (including rheumatoid arthritis, schizophrenia, older adults with complex conditions, cancer, multiple sclerosis, and inflammatory bowel disease)
research_question: This systematic review aims to identify and appraise published cost-effectiveness analyses of mobile device-based active remote monitoring technologies for people with long-term conditions, examining whether these interventions provide value compared to standard care in terms of costs and health outcomes.

comparison: Standard care without technology-based support interventions
intervention: Technology-based interventions including telehealth platforms, online portals, and mobile health applications
outcome: Symptom management effectiveness, emotional distress reduction, patient-provider communication enhancement, and identification of implementation barriers (digital literacy, device access)
population: Lung cancer patients undergoing treatment (pre-treatment, active treatment, and post-treatment phases)
research_question: This systematic review examines the role of technology-based interventions (including telehealth platforms, online portals, and mobile apps) in supporting lung cancer patients during their treatment journey, specifically investigating which technologies are utilized, how they address symptom management, emotional distress, and patient-provider communication, and what barriers patients encounter compared to standard care without technological support.

comparison: Different sociodemographic subgroups based on PROGRESS-Plus framework indicators (e.g., younger vs older adults, men vs women, high vs low socioeconomic status, different education levels)
intervention: Digital interventions targeting weight-related behaviors (diet, physical activity, sedentary behavior) and weight loss/maintenance
outcome: Intervention uptake, engagement, and effectiveness in promoting physical activity, healthy diet, reducing sedentary behavior, and weight loss/maintenance
population: Adults
research_question: This umbrella review examines whether there are social inequalities in the uptake, engagement, and effectiveness of digital interventions targeting weight-related behaviors (diet, physical activity, sedentary behavior) and weight loss maintenance in adults, comparing outcomes across different sociodemographic groups defined by PROGRESS-Plus framework indicators such as age, gender/sex, income, and education.

comparison: Demographic subgroups and varying levels of privacy, consent, and transparency conditions
exposure: Attitudes, perceptions, trust, privacy concerns, consent preferences, and transparency expectations regarding health data sharing
outcome: Willingness to share health data for secondary use (pooled proportion estimate)
population: General public/health consumers worldwide, predominantly from high-income countries
research_question: This meta-analysis examines what proportion of the global population is willing to share their health data for secondary purposes (such as research and quality improvement), and how willingness to share differs across demographic groups and is influenced by factors such as privacy concerns, consent, and transparency.

comparison: Standard care, no intervention, or baseline functioning without AI-assistive technology support
intervention: AI-assistive technologies including robotics, phone/computer applications, and virtual reality systems
outcome: Adaptive functioning outcomes including social skills, daily living skills, and communication abilities
population: Individuals with neurodevelopmental conditions (NDCs), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disabilities (ID), across different age groups with emphasis on children
research_question: This systematic review evaluates the efficacy and effectiveness of AI-assistive technologies in supporting adaptive functioning (including social skills, daily living skills, and communication) in individuals with neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disabilities, compared to standard care or no intervention, particularly in everyday settings such as homes, schools, and workplaces.

comparison: Traditional subjective clinical assessment methods and diagnostic approaches
exposure: Application of machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms for PTSD diagnosis and prediction
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and performance of machine learning models for PTSD detection (including model selection, feature identification, sample size considerations, and validation metrics)
population: Individuals with or at risk for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) who have experienced or witnessed traumatic events
research_question: This systematic review investigates whether machine learning approaches are effective and promising for automated diagnosis and prediction of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in individuals who have experienced or witnessed traumatic events, compared to traditional diagnostic methods, with outcomes measured by diagnostic accuracy and model performance metrics.

comparison: Conventional medical approaches or standard care without digital twins technology
intervention: Digital twins technology applications including personalized health management, precision individual therapy effects, and predicting individual risk
outcome: Patient health-related outcomes across 45 measured outcomes including personalized health management effectiveness, precision therapy effects, and individual risk prediction accuracy
population: Patients with various conditions including cancers, type 2 diabetes, multiple sclerosis, heart failure, qi deficiency, post-hepatectomy liver failure, and dental issues
research_question: This systematic review assesses the effectiveness of digital twins technology in improving health-related outcomes at the population level, examining whether digital twin-based interventions (including personalized health management, precision individual therapy effects, and predicting individual risk) can promote precision health across patients with various conditions compared to conventional care approaches.

comparison: Standard postoperative care without mobile or wearable digital health monitoring
intervention: Mobile and wearable digital health interventions (DHI) including wearable activity trackers, mobile phone applications, real-time collection of patient-reported outcomes, and digital health kits
outcome: Postoperative patient outcomes including complications, recovery status, patient-reported symptoms and signs, and methodological reporting quality assessed using mERA guidelines
population: Patients undergoing any surgery requiring skin incision, following hospital discharge
research_question: This systematic review examines the current use, evidence base, and methodological reporting quality of mobile devices and wearable digital health interventions (DHI) for measuring patient outcomes in the postoperative period following surgery, compared to standard postoperative care without digital monitoring.

comparison: Standard or non-inclusive digital health technology implementation without specific equity-focused strategies
intervention: Digital inclusivity strategies including outreach programmes, co-design approaches, user-friendly designs, supportive infrastructure provision, and educational support for digital literacy
outcome: Facilitators and barriers to digital health technology access, motivation, and use; identification of effective strategies for promoting digital inclusivity including user-friendly designs, supportive infrastructure, and educational support
population: Underserved groups experiencing digital exclusion, including those with low income, limited English fluency, homeless individuals, older adults, people with visual or hearing impairments, and those in rural areas
research_question: This systematic review synthesizes qualitative evidence on what key strategies have been used to promote digital inclusivity in health technologies for underserved groups, and assesses the facilitators and barriers to implementing and adopting these strategies in practice based on underserved groups' experiences and perspectives.

comparison: Control conditions, waitlist controls, or usual care (as reported in the 32 trials reviewed)
intervention: Automated digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) delivered via technology such as mobile applications, computers, text messaging services, or the Internet in Chinese language
outcome: Mental health symptom reduction, intervention efficacy/effectiveness, public accessibility, and implementation status of digital mental health interventions
population: Individuals with mental health symptoms or conditions (including depression, anxiety, and other mental disorders) in the Greater China region (mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan)
research_question: This scoping review aims to identify and evaluate the efficacy of automated digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) available in Chinese language within the Greater China region (mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan), assess their public accessibility, and identify gaps in research and implementation for individuals with mental health symptoms.

comparison: Standard care, usual care, or control conditions without app-based interventions
intervention: Mobile phone or tablet application (app)-based health interventions, including integrated or stand-alone health apps for disease management, lifestyle monitoring, medication adherence, and symptom tracking
outcome: Medication adherence, laboratory parameters, anthropometric parameters, functional parameters, symptom scores, quality of life, and healthcare resource utilization
population: Patients with various health conditions including diabetes, anxiety, depression, and other chronic diseases
research_question: This umbrella review aims to systematically map and summarize the existing evidence from systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials investigating the effectiveness and efficacy of mobile phone or tablet app-based health interventions in improving health outcomes across various patient populations compared to standard care or control conditions.

comparison: No intervention/passive interventions, traditional cognitive training, traditional exercises
intervention: Serious games (including exergames and cognitive training games)
outcome: Attention performance (focused attention, sustained attention, alternating attention, selective attention, divided attention)
population: Cognitively impaired older adults (elderly individuals with cognitive disorders such as dementia, Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment)
research_question: This meta-analysis examines whether serious games are effective in enhancing attention in cognitively impaired older adults compared to no intervention/passive interventions, traditional cognitive training, or traditional exercises.

comparison: Standard heart failure care without wearable remote monitoring
exposure: Use of noninvasive wearable devices for remote monitoring (including smartwatches, rings, and clothing-incorporated accessories)
outcome: Clinical readiness of wearables (Medical Device Readiness Level), regulatory approval status (FDA/MDR classification), impact on mortality and hospitalization rates, and validity for heart failure management
population: Heart failure patients
research_question: This scoping review aims to summarize the current evidence on wearable devices for remote monitoring of heart failure patients, assess their functionalities and applications, and evaluate their developmental readiness for clinical practice using the Medical Device Readiness Level framework and regulatory classifications.
